current_episode.title: Cintoo, the Netflix for 3D Data with Dominique Pouliquen

guest.bio_context: Dominique Pouliquen joined Autodesk through the acquisition of his first company, RealViz, a spin-off from a French lab developing photogrammetry technology for extracting 3D from 2D pictures. At Autodesk, he co-led the ReCap team in San Francisco, building software to manage massive point cloud data and democratizing access to point clouds across Revit, AutoCAD, and C3D. He left Autodesk to co-found Cintoo with PhDs from another French lab who had developed compression technology to make point cloud data cloud-accessible and streamable in web browsers.

key_stats: 110,000+ active users on the Cintoo platform
Data compression ratio of 20 to 1 (reducing file size by 20 times)
Approximately 10 years ago: period when Autodesk ReCap was managing point clouds with desktop-centric workflows
60-70% of U.S. construction business is renovation work
Seven to eight years ago: introduction of red and green QA/QC visualization in Cintoo
context.transcript_excerpt: So the core technology we got from my co-founders, PhDs, was this capacity to turn a huge point cloud into compressed data. The way they do that is by turning that into 3D mesh or 3D surfaces. And that will solve another problem we had with point cloud. Point cloud is like a 3D dot in space. So you see through the dots. It's not continuous information. but the world we are looking at is made of surfaces. You don't see through the walls. So by turning point cloud into 3D surfaces, I was also pretty convinced that this would be a much easier way to interpret your point cloud data. So two aspects here. First, we could compress it by turning it into meshes. Secondly, the 3D surface you get or the 3D mesh you get will make the data much easier to view and interpret. And last but not least, the core technology also includes the fact that we can stream these high-resolution 3D meshes, which are at the resolution of the source scan, in a web browser using fast streaming. pending_qa.q: What specific value proposition does a shared reality capture platform provide to fragmented construction teams beyond documentation?
pending_qa.r: Beyond better documentation and scan-to-BIM efficiency, the platform provides a shared source of truth across fragmented teams, enabling faster decision-making and higher confidence in decisions against real-world conditions. The unlimited user policy allows companies to invite as many team members as needed across disciplines and permissioning allows access to certain areas only. This prevents knowledge from staying isolated in one virtual BIM manager's head and transforms it into industrial knowledge accessible to all stakeholders, giving teams earlier visibility into divergence between design intent and actual as-built conditions.
